institutionName: Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU)

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to be sure that I was in a country where the academic standard was high - as we know it is in the Nordics. It was important for me to gain professional knowledge as well as personal experiences from my exchange stay. Furthermore, I wanted to be in a country with beautiful nature.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I loved my exchange stay, it taught me a lot on a personal level

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was a bit difficult because the summer holiday period overlapped in Denmark and Norway, so when I had questions I had no one to go to for 6 weeks.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Only the orientation week, the office for exchange students was not really helpfull

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I think it was difficult in the beginning because there was no personal help to be had. Everything had to be read from a paper given by NTNU.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
It was easy.
Finn.no
or Facebook was really helpfull. It is a huge thing to rent rooms in Norway, so if you ain't interested in living on campus with 10-12 others,
Finn.no
is a good option.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is very easy to get around by bus, (okay prices). In the beginning it is difficult because you don't know the city, after a while it was great to live a little away from the city center and snow came early a little outside the city!!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The prices are the same as in Copenhagen, Denmark

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was difficult to find Master subjects. It was not possible to check this off on NTNU's website, which meant that I had to read about all the subjects I found interesting in order to know the level (Bachelor or Master).

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
First, you need to find an area that suits your study-direction at your home university. Next, read about the subjects and find out whether they are qualified, then you have to check the language. Important: Check exam dates, as you are responsible for knowing that the subjects do not overlap.
End: You should apply to join the course (maybe you will get it, maybe not - of not, then you have to find a new subject).

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Only the NTNU homepage, with an overview of all courses.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got 2 out of 4 applied courses. And I therefore had to go through the registration process again

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Check the exam period! It is super important. And consider whether you can find courses worth 15 ECTS points, as there is much else new then you are at exchanges in a new country. Finally, I was lucky to have a 15 ECTS course which took place over 1 week from 09 to 15 every day - that gave me a lot of freedom.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It is the same as in Denmark

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It was good, the same as we know from Denmark

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The same, only difference is the grading system (A-F). Otherwise, everything is pretty much the same.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *

questions.answer: Food was really expensive, especially meat.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I signed up for tennis/padel and I loved it! It was a wonderful way to get to know new people

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All options, there is everything one could wish for through NTNUI

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Tennis/padel was fun

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Experience the crazy nature
and then it is "Endelig Mandag" which gives the opportunity to eat good gourmet food in the city

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I lived with 2 Norwegian girls, and thereby I met and socialized with other Norwegian people. In addition, tennis/padel was a good way to get to know the locals

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: They are not good at irony, very political correct and they are not so open to strangers

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: That they are incredibly calm and good at doing local things

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Think about your housing situation (room, roommates or alone)

Norway is a very expensive country

Try as much as you can to socialize at the beginning and make some friends

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Use the ATB-app for transport 
The app "All Trails" can show you good and not searchable hiking tours in the local area

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting friends all over the world

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The beginning was hard on me. It was hard to be in a new country, new school, new home, new friends, new culture, new everything

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: no

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
